subject: Add-ons: observability credits, trace sampling & dashboard SKUs
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Brooks <emma.brooks@skyline-ai.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Add-ons: observability credits, trace sampling & dashboard SKUs

Emma — following up from our demo last week. Attached is a compact pricing matrix that shows the add-on SKUs we discussed (retention tiers, tracing sampling, and dashboard seats). High level:

- 90-day retention (default): unit-priced per GB-month
- 1-year retention: 0.6x unit price vs default, commitment required
- Tracing: charged per sampled span, with a SKU for 100% sampling vs 25%/50% sampling profiles
- Dashboards: base seat + premium widget pack (advanced visualizations / long-retain query cache)

A couple of items we should clarify for Skyline before we formalize pricing:
1) Desired retention SLAs and whether you need warm/nearline retrieval for >90 days
2) Trace sampling target — you mentioned wanting full traces on anomaly windows only; we have a dynamic-sampling policy that can cut costs but may change billable spans
3) Billing model — annual committed credits vs monthly metered (we can propose blended pricing)

I attached: pricing_matrix_SKYLINE_Q4.xlsx and a SOW-draft-SKYLINE.pdf for a quick read. Can you confirm: procurement contact, desired commit length (12/24 months), and whether Skyline will want the premium dashboard widget pack?

If useful, we can propose a swap: move some of your compute commit into observability credits (reduces per-token cost by ~7.5% but increases observability retention discounts).

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Emma Brooks <emma.brooks@skyline-ai.com>

Subject: Re: Add-ons: observability credits, trace sampling & dashboard SKUs

Jonas — thanks for this. Quick clarifications from our side (procurement joined):

- Commitment: We are evaluating between 12 and 24 months; procurement prefers annual but needs price certainty.
- Retention: We must keep traces and logs for 12 months for some audit workflows (we can tier cold storage after 90 days, but retrieval SLA can be relaxed).
- Sampling: We currently run 100% sampling on a subset of inference flows (model debugging). We would like a policy that allows 100% for flagged windows but 10% baseline otherwise.
- Dashboards: We want the premium widget pack for the SRE team (up to 6 seats).

Two asks from procurement before we move to legal:
1) Can you provide a worked example invoice for a mixed sampling policy (10% baseline + 100% for flagged windows) and 12-month retention with cold-tier after 90 days?
2) Any flexibility on observability credits if we commit to a 24-month deal?

I've attached our security questionnaire for reference. Procurement: feel free to chime in.

— Emma
Emma Brooks | Head of Observability, Skyline AI

Team — forwarding Skyline's asks. Key negotiation levers they want: 12 vs 24 month commit, tracing sampling profile, and premium dashboards for 6 seats. They specifically asked for a worked invoice example showing mixed sampling.

Proposed options to discuss:
- Option A (12m): Baseline 10% sampling + flagged windows 100% (meter spans). Observability credit multiplier: x1.0, retention 12 months with cold-tier after 90 days at 0.35x retrieval cost. No extra discount.
- Option B (24m commit): Move 15% of compute commit to observability credits -> observability multiplier x0.75 and provide a one-time credit equal to 2 months of dashboard fees. Also unlock premium widget pack price at $X/seat.

Notes/questions:
- Can we flex on the swap percentage? If we take 12% instead of 15% of compute commit, what changes in their blended unit economics?
- Any redlines on SOW that we should pre-empt?

Marissa — you're best to own pricing math. Ben — can you sketch the invoice example? Lauren — any commercial guardrails we should apply here?

— Jonas

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emma Brooks <emma.brooks@skyline-ai.com>, procurement@skyline-ai.com
Date: 2026-12-02T09:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Add-ons: observability credits, trace sampling & dashboard SKUs

Quick draft numbers (see attached pricing_counter_SKYLINE.xlsx):

- Scenario: 12-month baseline commit, expected monthly usage: 2 TB retention-equivalent, trace spans baseline 10% (~200M spans/mo), flagged windows add ~50M spans/mo during anomalies. Dashboard: 6 premium seats.

Metered invoice example (12m):
- Observability storage (90d hot then cold): $0.032/GB-month hot, $0.011/GB-month cold (applies after 90d); approx $6,400/mo
- Trace spans: baseline sampled spans (10%): $1,600/mo; flagged windows (extra 50M spans): $400/mo; total $2,000/mo
- Dashboards premium: $120/seat/mo -> $720/mo
- Total monthly: ~$9,120

Offer: For 12m commit, provide a 7% discount on observability storage and waive setup for dashboard migration (one-time).

Counter (24m swap option):
- If Skyline swaps 12% of compute commit into observability credits (24m), unit prices drop: storage - 18% off, span unit price - 25% off, dashboard seats - $95/seat/mo. Additionally offer one-time 2-month credit on dashboard fees. Net monthly: ~$6,900 (approx).

We should keep the swap conservative — 12% looks like a safe middle ground to protect gross margin while giving clear economics to the customer. Legal: SOW changes limited to the observability addendum and a clause on trace-sampling billing (we charge actual sampled spans; dynamic-sampling policy must be documented).

Attachments: pricing_counter_SKYLINE.xlsx (worked invoice examples and math).

— Ben
Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Emma / procurement team — thanks for the quick turn. Based on internal review we've prepared two concrete offers (see summary below) and attached the worked invoice. If either looks good I can get this to legal for a short addendum and we can schedule a kickoff for migrations.

Offer 1 — 12-month (metered, small discount)
- Baseline sampling 10% + flagged windows at 100% (we bill actual sampled spans)
- 12-month retention with cold-tier after 90d (cold retrieval SLA: 48 hours)
- 7% discount on observability storage fees; dashboard migration setup waived
- No compute swap required
- Estimated monthly: ~$9.1k (per Ben's worked invoice)

Offer 2 — 24-month (swap + deeper discounts)
- Swap 12% of compute commit into observability credits (applied over 24 months)
- Storage -18% unit price, span price -25% unit price, dashboard seats $95/seat/mo
- One-time 2-month credit on dashboard fees
- Commitment: 24 months; observability credits applied monthly
- Estimated monthly-equivalent: ~$6.9k after credits

Next steps: which offer do you prefer? If 24-month swap, procurement asked for the commit-to-credit worksheet (we can provide the amortization table). I'm happy to schedule a 30-min call tomorrow to walk through the invoice and the swap mechanics.

If you confirm one, I'll:
- push the addendum to legal (we'll include a trace-sampling billing appendix)
- attach the commit-to-credit worksheet and amortization (for procurement)
- set up a technical kickoff for dashboard migration (Marissa will own delivery)

Best — Jonas
